forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Vale of White Horse investment returns ahead of budget as deposit rates beat forecast
news_drafts.lead: The Vale of White Horse council expects to receive £1.146m more in investment income than budgeted for 2026–27, driven by higher returns on its treasury deposits, the cabinet heard this week. The council's cash reserves are earning 4.26 per cent on average, outperforming the government's Sterling Overnight Index Average benchmark of 3.74 per cent. However, the council is also forecasting a £698,000 overspend on employee costs in the first quarter, largely because of spending on staff for the local government reorganisation programme, project surveyors and temporary legal cover. A £0.7m underspend on disabled facilities grants, which fund home adaptations for disabled people, is under national review by the Department for Health and Social Care, and the council risks having to return unspent money.

news_drafts.headline: Vale of White Horse council's investment income beats budget by £1.146m
news_drafts.lead: Vale of White Horse Council's investment income is forecast to reach £5.66 million, beating budget by £1.146 million. The outperformance comes from higher returns on deposits — averaging 4.26 per cent against a 3.74 per cent benchmark — according to June monitoring figures presented to the Cabinet. The windfall helps offset pressures from employee costs, forecast to overspend by £698,000, largely through reorganisation work and staffing for major property projects. The council is also managing a predicted £700,000 underspend on disabled facilities grants, which are under national department review.

findings.headline: Disabled Facilities Grant underspend of £0.7m under national department review, with risk of clawback
findings.detail: The council is predicting a £0.7m underspend against the DFG budget based on first-quarter spend. The Department for Health and Social Care are currently reviewing DFG underspends nationally. The housing team are working with partner agencies to reduce the underspend.
findings.matters: A national review of DFG underspends raises the risk of clawback or reduced future allocations, which could constrain the council's ability to support disabled residents' adaptations and may signal funding pressure across the sector.
findings.figures: £0.7m DFG underspend predicted; spending will continue through the year
findings.quote: Disabled facilities grant is underspent and whilst spend will continue through the year we are predicting a £0.7 million underspend against budget... The Department for Health and Social Care are currently reviewing DFG underspends

findings.headline: Employee costs overspent by £698k in first quarter, driven by reorganisation work and project staffing
findings.detail: The council is overrunning on personnel costs across multiple areas: Corporate Services for local government reorganisation work, Development and Corporate Landlord surveyors for major property projects, Finance additional resources for long-term absence, and expensive locum legal staff. These are partially offset by vacancies in the planning policy team.
findings.matters: A £698k overspend in one quarter (25% of the year) suggests either structural cost pressures or temporary one-off activity; if structural, this could erode the investment income advantage by year end. LGR work is presumably time-bounded but may extend.
findings.figures: £698k employee cost overspend; service-level overspend of £510k (excluding investment income)
findings.quote: As at the end of June 2026, employee costs are forecast to be overspent by 698,000

findings.headline: Investment income forecast £1.146m ahead of budget, driven by higher treasury deposit returns
findings.detail: The council's treasury investments are outperforming budget significantly. Net investment interest is forecast to be £5.66m against the budget of £4.514m. The actual average rate of return on internally managed treasury deposits was 4.26 per cent, outperforming the SONIA benchmark of 3.74 per cent.
findings.matters: A £1.146m windfall is material to the council's bottom line, but the forecast depends on continued high interest rates; the treasury advisor's forecast shows no reductions forecast until September 2027, so this benefit may reverse when the MPC cuts.
findings.figures: £5.66m forecast investment income vs £4.514m budgeted; actual rate of return 4.26% vs SONIA benchmark 3.74%
findings.quote: net investment interest is forecast to be £5.66 million against the current budget of £4.514 million

findings.headline: Multiple capital projects show cost overruns requiring budget coverage in 2026/27
findings.detail: Beyond the decarbonisation overspend, Sparsholt Sewage Works (YA46) has a £10,207 overspend and Faringdon Artificial Turf Pitch (YC67) has a £4,256 overspend, both marked for future budget coverage. This pattern suggests systemic cost control issues across the capital programme.
findings.matters: Multiple overspends across different project types indicate potential project management weaknesses and create cumulative forward budget liabilities
findings.figures: YA46: £10,207 overspend; YC67: £4,256 overspend; YC91: £900,434 overspend
findings.quote: YA46 Sparsholt Sewage Works 0 10,207 10,207 Carry forward overspend to be covered by budget in 2026/27

findings.headline: Wantage Leisure Centre decarbonisation overspent by £900k, with cost overrun to be covered from 2026/27 budget
findings.detail: The Wantage LC Decarbonisation project (YC91) spent £2,527,202 against a budget of £1,626,768, generating a £900,434 overspend. The variance explanation explicitly states this overspend 'is to be covered by budget in 2026/27', creating a forward liability.
findings.matters: Major capital project cost overruns indicate cost control weaknesses and create budget pressures that constrain financial flexibility in the following year
findings.quote: YC91 Wantage LC - Decarbonisation 1,626,768 2,527,202 900,434 Carry forward overspend to be covered by budget in 2026/27
